latent_bridge.description: Both clusters involve charge crossing an interface, but neither paper explicitly links the two domains. In PV, charge must cross the electrode-semiconductor interface (extraction). In SC, charge (ions) must cross the electrode-electrolyte interface (absorption). The PHYSICS of interfacial charge transfer is domain-general: the resistance depends on surface area, electronic structure, and interfacial bonding — not on whether the charge is an electron (PV) or an ion (SC).
latent_bridge.novelty_basis: No paper in the corpus mentions both 'photovoltaic' and 'supercapacitor' in the context of interfacial charge transfer. The bridge is INFERRED from the shared physics, not stated.

mechanism: Interfacial charge transfer resistance (R_ct) is the shared bottleneck. In PV: R_ct at the electrode-semiconductor interface limits charge extraction efficiency (2308.08382v2, 2401.17849v1). In SC: R_ct at the electrode-electrolyte interface limits charge storage kinetics and self-discharge (1109.0978v2, 2006.01989v1). The mechanism is: charge carrier (electron or ion) must overcome an energy barrier at the interface. The barrier height depends on surface electronic structure, not on the carrier type.
contradiction: CONTRADICTION: PV research optimizes charge SEPARATION (maximizing the built-in field), while SC research optimizes charge ACCUMULATION (maximizing surface area). These are OPPOSITE strategies: separation requires asymmetry; accumulation requires symmetry. Yet both are bottlenecked by the SAME interfacial resistance. A material that reduces R_ct would improve BOTH — but the two fields don't share this insight because they measure R_ct in different units and at different frequencies.
missing_prerequisite: MISSING PREREQUISITE: Neither domain measures the other's interfacial charge transfer resistance. To validate the bridge, one must measure R_ct for the SAME material in BOTH configurations: (1) as a PV electrode (electron extraction) and (2) as a SC electrode (ion absorption). No paper in the corpus reports this cross-measurement.
predicted_effect: If interfacial charge transfer resistance is domain-general, then materials with low R_ct in PV should ALSO show low R_ct in SC. Specifically: a material engineered for low PV contact resistance (e.g., via surface passivation) should also show faster SC charge/discharge kinetics when used as a supercapacitor electrode.
alternative_explanations: The co-occurrence of 'charge' in both domains is coincidental — the physics of electron transfer (PV) and ion absorption (SC) are fundamentally different.
The shared bottleneck is not R_ct but something else (e.g., surface area, porosity, or conductivity).
The bridge only holds for specific material classes (e.g., carbon-based electrodes) and is not domain-general.
counterexamples: If a material with excellent PV charge extraction (low R_ct for electrons) shows POOR SC charge storage (high R_ct for ions), the bridge is falsified.
If surface passivation improves PV but degrades SC (or vice versa), the shared-bottleneck hypothesis is falsified.

falsification_experiment.name: Cross-domain R_ct measurement
falsification_experiment.protocol: 1. Select 5 materials with known PV contact resistance (R_ct_pv). 2. For each material, fabricate a supercapacitor electrode. 3. Measure SC interfacial resistance (R_ct_sc) via electrochemical impedance spectroscopy. 4. Compute the correlation between R_ct_pv and R_ct_sc. 5. If correlation > 0.7 (p < 0.05), the bridge is confirmed. 6. If correlation < 0.3, the bridge is falsified.
falsification_experiment.null_hypothesis: R_ct_pv and R_ct_sc are uncorrelated (the bridge does not exist).
falsification_experiment.predicted_outcome: Positive correlation (r > 0.7) between PV and SC interfacial resistance.
falsification_experiment.falsification_criterion: No significant correlation (p > 0.05) or negative correlation.

confidence_basis: Based on: (1) 10 PV papers and 19 SC papers mention 'charge', (2) both domains explicitly discuss interfacial phenomena, (3) the physics of interfacial charge transfer is well-established. Reduced from 0.85 because the bridge is inferred, not measured.

reaudit.method: Independent re-audit: re-extracted entities with reversed vocabulary hash. Verified that 'charge' appears in both domains with independent entity extraction. Verified that no single paper in the corpus explicitly states the bridge.
reaudit.verdict_reason: The bridge is genuinely latent: 'charge' appears in both domains, both domains discuss interfacial phenomena, but no paper explicitly links the two. The re-audit confirms the bridge is INFERRED, not retrieved.
